caption: The image is a technical drawing on beige-toned paper that shows the design elements for a "banjo clock." There are two main sections on the sheet. At the top, labeled "FACE DESIGN," is a circular clock face with the Roman numerals XII and VI at the top and bottom and two simple tick marks at 3 and 9 o'clock positions. The clock face includes decorative artwork in the center: an oval frame with the text “CHAPIN LITTLE FALLS.” Within the inner design, there are landscape elements, trees, buildings, a river or lake, and a sailing boat. At the top right, the text reads "BANJO CLOCK ONEIDA HISTORICAL SOCIETY UTICA, N.Y." In the lower section, labeled "BASE DESIGN," there is a rectangular panel with a depiction of a seated female figure in a dress, holding a shield patterned with stripes and stars. She points with her right hand toward an eagle with spread wings. The background contains stylized clouds and a landscape. Ornamental corner designs decorate the rectangle's border. On the left side, a note indicates that the flag depicted in the image has 16 stars and specifies “6” SQUARE GLASS.” The entire sheet is monochromatic, primarily drawn with fine pencil or ink lines on a solid beige background.
title: Banjo Clock
